doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Decline of Disney's music program
summary: Disney's entertainment division was absorbed by operations and the band shrank.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: they didn’t need all this entertainment. And it’s too bad. And I saw it from a business perspective. I saw it happening because when Disney opened, this was October 1, 1971, they had an autonomous entertainment division, with a vice president, you know, a board, I mean boy we could do anything and get anything. And I saw over a period of about two years the entertainment division completely absorbed by operations. It just disappeared.

And you know the 20-piece band went down to 12, which now, and it’s a good bunch of guys. I couldn’t do it. It’d kill me you know. But I mean it’s oh, a lot of choreography and no reeds just all high trumpets and a lot of loud you know — and — but that’s all they have in the Magic Kingdom. Now thank God for the World Showcase in EPCOT because they have a lot of international entertainment there, which they have to have. But I mean there were so many musicians in the Magic Kingdom alone. Little bands on the street corner if you’re waiting in line there’s somebody to entertain you.
